notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-55: f=xy²(4−x−y). Interior stationary point(1,2) gives4. On axes f=0; on x+y=6, f=−2xy², minimized at(2,4) with−64. Include the other interior critical boundary-axis cases.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-56: Writing r²=x²+y² gives0≤f≤2r²e^(−r²)≤2/e, attained at r=1 with x=0. Nonnegative f vanishes only at the origin.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-58: f_x=−4x−8y gives x=−2y. Then f_y=0 reduces to2y³−8y−5=0. The Hessian determinant is48y²−64 and f_xx=−4. Compare the two maximum heights; completing the square shows f→−∞ at infinity.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-59: On the unit circle x²=1−y², maximize/minimize y−y³ on−1≤y≤1. Critical y=±1/√3 gives the extrema.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-60: Set u=1/x,v=1/y. Then u²+v²=1 and f=u+v; the extrema±√2 occur at u=v=±1/√2, allowed by x,y≠0.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-61: Under x²+y²+z²=3, AM–GM on the three squared coordinates gives |xyz|≤1; equality when |x|=|y|=|z|=1.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-62: The constraints give y=(z−1)/2 and x=3(1−z)/2. Substituting gives 23*z^2/4 - 11*z/2 + 11/4, minimized at z=11/23. The positive quadratic is unbounded above.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-63: At a minimum, x²:y²:z²=1:2:3 from the logarithmic constraint. With y²=2x²,z²=3x² and xz>0, the product constraint gives x²=1/√3. Four sign choices remain.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-64: At optimum L+2w+2h=108. For fixed girth a square cross-section maximizes area; maximize L(108−L)²/16 at L=36.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-review-65: Let base b=2a cosθ, vertical height h=(P−b−2a)/2. Area=bh+(b/2)a sinθ. Interior optimization gives θ=π/6 and a=P/(3+2√3), b=√3a, h=(1+√3)a/2; compare degenerate boundaries.
